newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia may loosen property rules for foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia may loosen property rules for foreigners.

text.p: Malaysia is considering the relaxation of property purchase restrictions on foreigners, Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Friday.
He said he has asked the Foreign Investment Committee (FIC) to consider allowing foreigners to buy commercial and residential property within city limits.
The relaxation would not include allowing foreigners buying low-cost or low- and medium-cost properties that cater mainly to the domestic market, he said.
"I've asked the FIC to liberalise the guidelines to ensure there is a bigger market...to allow for the foreign interests to buy," Anwar said in a speech at a building groundbreaking ceremony.
Anwar noted that current FIC guidelines "disallow foreign interests to hold offices or condos within city limits".
"We did introduce those measures at a difficult time," he added. Malaysia imposed restrictions on foreign property buyers in 1995 to curb property speculation.
He later told reporters the current 100,000 ringgit levy imposed on foreigners buying Malaysian real estate "can still be imposed, but probably for the real up-market (properties)".

Asked if the possible relaxation of property rules was meant to revive the property market, which has been dampened by central bank curbs on lending to the sector, Anwar said, "Not necessarily to revive (it), because I think it is still sustainable right now."
But, he conceded, "the developers are telling us that the guidelines are actually inhibiting the growth".

Malaysia's central Bank Negara Malaysia, fearing a speculative property bubble like Thailand's, imposed measures effective on April 1 to limit lending in the sector to 20 percent of a bank's outstanding loans.
